title: Picard norm for a finite field extension and scheme pullback
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $K/k$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-field-tower] of degree $d=[K:k]\geq1$. For every $k$-scheme $Z$ [def-pc-scheme] put $Z_K=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $p_Z:Z_K\to Z$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(W)$ for the isomorphism classes $[A]$ of invertible $\mathcal O_W$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], with tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback] induces the maps denoted by $h^*$ on these classes. There are maps
$$\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Z}:\operatorname{Pic}(Z_K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$$
with the following properties. They preserve tensor products and the structure-sheaf class. For every invertible module $A$ on $Z$,
$$\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Z}([p_Z^*A])=[A^{\otimes d}].$$
For every morphism of $k$-schemes $h:W\to Z$, let $h_K:W_K\to Z_K$ be its base change [def-pc-base-change]. For every invertible module $F$ on $Z_K$ one has
$$h^*\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Z}([F])=\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,W}([h_K^*F]).$$
No separability, smoothness, finite-type, separatedness, reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on this norm assertion.

source.place: Tags 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), and 0BUT (lemma-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs). The line-class base-change clause follows by applying the arbitrary-base-change assertion of 0BD2 to the transition functions in the proof of 0BCY.

proof.text: Fix once for all a $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $K$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of any $k$-scheme $Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify $p_Z^{-1}U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_k K)$. The elements $1\otimes b_a$ form an $R$-basis: the maps $R^d\to R\otimes_k K$, $(r_a)\mapsto\sum_a r_a\otimes b_a$, and $r\otimes x\mapsto(r\lambda_a(x))_a$ are inverse, where $\lambda_a$ are the coordinate functionals of the chosen basis. Thus $p_Z$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. These coordinate isomorphisms commute with restrictions between affine opens: restriction sends $r\otimes x$ to $(r|_{U'})\otimes x$, by the projection formulas in the affine fibre-product statement. For a general open $V\subseteq Z$, decompose a section on $p_Z^{-1}V$ on an affine cover of $V$. On affine refinements of the overlaps uniqueness of its $d$ coordinates makes the local coefficients agree; the sheaf axiom glues them. This gives, on every $V$, mutually inverse restriction-compatible maps $\Gamma(p_Z^{-1}V,\mathcal O)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)^d$. In particular no affine-intersection assumption is needed.

proof.text:
For $c\in\Gamma(p_Z^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ write $c(1\otimes b_a)=\sum_t M_V(c)_{ta}(1\otimes b_t)$ using step 1, and define $
u_{Z,V}(c)=\det M_V(c)$. All coefficients restrict, so these maps commute with restriction. The multiplication matrices satisfy $M_V(cc')=M_V(c)M_V(c')$; multiplicativity of the determinant in [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities], with $n=d\geq1$, gives $
u(cc')=
u(c)
u(c')$. In the determinant expansion of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the identity matrix has determinant $1$ and the scalar matrix $aI_d$ has determinant $a^d$: all nonidentity permutations have a zero off-diagonal factor. Consequently $
u(1)=1$ and $
u(p_Z^\sharp a)=a^d$. In particular $
u(u)$ is a unit when $u$ is a unit, since $
u(u)
u(u^{-1})=1$. Only these multiplicative and power identities will be used; a pointwise vanishing criterion is unnecessary.

proof.text: Let $F$ be invertible on $Z_K$. Since $p_Z$ is finite, [lem-sfb-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs] supplies an open cover $(V_i)$ of $Z$ and frames $e_i$ of $F$ on $p_Z^{-1}V_i$. Write $e_i=u_{ij}e_j$. Apply [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing] to $p_Z$ and the restriction-compatible multiplicative maps of step 2. Its hypotheses require no flatness or vanishing condition. It gives an invertible module $N$ on $Z$ and frames $f_i$ satisfying $f_i=\nu_Z(u_{ij})f_j$. We will define $\operatorname{Nm}_{K/k,Z}([F])=[N]$, after checking independence of the presentation in the next step.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction, specialized using one fixed k-basis of K; Tag 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), transition-function construction and its omitted verifications.

proof.text:
Compare two choices of cover and frames on their common refinement $(V_i\cap V'_j)$. Changing frames there from $e_i$ to $e'_i=a_i e_i$ changes the transitions to $u'_{ij}=a_i u_{ij}a_j^{-1}$. Multiplicativity gives $v'_{ij}=
u(a_i)v_{ij}
u(a_j)^{-1}$, where $v_{ij}=
u(u_{ij})$. Hence the local isomorphisms $f'_i\mapsto
u(a_i)f_i$ agree on overlaps: both images of $f'_i=v'_{ij}f'_j$ are $
u(a_i)v_{ij}f_j$. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] glues these maps and their inverses to inverse global maps. Refining a cover just restricts its transition equations, so the same argument also compares the original two covers. If $F\simeq F'$, transport the frames through this isomorphism; their transitions are identical. Thus the construction depends only on $[F]$ and defines the displayed map.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction, specialized using one fixed k-basis of K; Tag 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), transition-function construction and its omitted verifications.

proof.text: For invertible $F,G$ choose a common cover trivializing both upstairs. Their tensor product is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1). The frame $e_i\otimes g_i$ has transition $u_{ij}w_{ij}$: this follows from bilinearity [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; it is a frame by tensoring the two frame isomorphisms and the unit isomorphism $\mathcal O\otimes\mathcal O\simeq\mathcal O$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal]. The restriction comparisons needed here are the open-immersion case of (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Its norm therefore has transition $\nu(u_{ij})\nu(w_{ij})$, the same as $N(F)\otimes N(G)$. The maps between the corresponding tensor frames glue to an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1). For the structure sheaf take its global frame $1$; all transitions and their norms are $1$, and the resulting frame maps glue it to $\mathcal O_Z$. This proves both multiplicativity assertions.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction, specialized using one fixed k-basis of K; Tag 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), transition-function construction and its omitted verifications.

proof.text: Choose local frames $a_i$ of an invertible module $A$ on $Z$, with transitions $\alpha_{ij}$. Tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback] sends the frame isomorphism to a frame $p_Z^*a_i$ of $p_Z^*A$, whose transition is $p_Z^\sharp\alpha_{ij}$; invertibility is also asserted by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1). Step 2 makes its norm transition $\alpha_{ij}^d$. The tensor-power assertion of [lem-sfb-norm-frame-tensor-section-gluing], applied with $p=\mathrm{id}_Z$, $\nu=\mathrm{id}$, $M=A$, $n=d\geq1$, gives frames $a_i^{\otimes d}$ of $A^{\otimes d}$ with exactly these transitions. Matching the norm frames with these tensor frames and using [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1) gives $N(p_Z^*A)\simeq A^{\otimes d}$.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction, specialized using one fixed k-basis of K; Tag 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), transition-function construction and its omitted verifications.

proof.text: For $h:W\to Z$ and an open $V\subseteq Z$, write $h^\sharp$ and $h_K^\sharp$ for pullback of regular functions to the inverse-image opens. We claim $h^\sharp\nu_{Z,V}(c)=\nu_{W,h^{-1}V}(h_K^\sharp c)$. It suffices to restrict to affine opens $T\subseteq h^{-1}U$, with $U\subseteq V$ affine. The fibre-product identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] turn $h_K^\sharp$ into $R\otimes_k K\to S\otimes_k K$, $r\otimes x\mapsto h^\sharp(r)\otimes x$, where $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$ and $S=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O)$. It preserves the fixed basis $1\otimes b_a$, so the multiplication matrix becomes $(h^\sharp(M_U(c)_{ta}))_{ta}$. Applying a ring map to the finite sum $\det M=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_a M_{a,\sigma(a)}$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives the determinant of this new matrix. This proves the claimed equality on $T$; these $T$ cover $h^{-1}V$, so the sheaf equality axiom proves it globally. This is a polynomial identity over arbitrary commutative rings and requires no flatness of $h$.

source.place: Tag 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction, specialized using one fixed k-basis of K; Tag 0BCY (lemma-norm-invertible), transition-function construction and its omitted verifications.

proof.text: Use the cover and frames for $F$ from step 3. By [def-pc-module-pullback] the pullback $h_K^*F$ has frames $h_K^*e_i$ over $p_W^{-1}(h^{-1}V_i)$, with transitions $h_K^\sharp u_{ij}$. Here the two inverse-image opens agree by $p_Zh_K=hp_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1), both $h_K^*F$ and $h^*N(F)$ are invertible. Their norm and pullback frames have transitions respectively $\nu_W(h_K^\sharp u_{ij})$ and $h^\sharp\nu_Z(u_{ij})$; these are equal by step 7. Matching these frames gives local isomorphisms that agree on every overlap, and [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1) glues them and their inverses. Thus $h^*N(F)\simeq N(h_K^*F)$ and the asserted equality of Picard classes follows. All constructions use the same fixed basis of $K/k$ for every $Z$. Empty schemes cause no exception: the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives the unique module class and all equalities; for $d=1$ the matrices are $1\times1$. Nilpotents and inseparability do not affect any calculation.
